question: Why does adsorption of surfactants tend to occur on inner surfaces of double-layer graphene compared to outer surfaces?
answer: Adsorption of surfactants preferentially occurs on inner surfaces of double-layer graphene due to dehydration between graphene layers, which enhances hydrophilic interactions between surfactant molecules and graphene surfaces. This facilitates stronger adsorption on inner surfaces compared to outer surfaces.
